samples.text: While the incident remains open, the period is carried on a manual basis: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. That override is the holding position, and it replaces the automated mapping step rather than repairing it. The basis for it is the cause confirmed so far, recorded as stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Measured against a normal run, the gap is one of assurance rather than output. The valuation can be produced, but each mapped code now depends on a person checking it instead of on a maintained reference. For teams deciding whether to wait, the provisional answer is that waiting is reasonable for consumers of period totals and not for owners of the mapping. The override buys time, yet it leaves the failed reference data unchanged, so any run that starts before the register is corrected will meet the same condition. This position covers the current period only and gives no protection to the next scheduled run. Until

The valuation failed because of stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. That cause is confirmed, not inferred, and every later finding in this review rests on it. At the start of the incident the working explanation was different: it was initially recorded as overnight ERP outage. That hypothesis was ruled out on direct evidence, namely ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window, which removed the upstream system from the frame and sent the investigation back to the reference data. On review, the root cause behind the product hierarchy sync service is classed as control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer. Put plainly, the stale mapping was the trigger, and the missing control is the reason a stale entry could sit unnoticed until a valuation run depended on it.
